p.x:
Being "high agency" seems to presuppose that agency is a unitary personality characteristic but that doesn't seem to be the case to me? Like, how agency usually gets defined it seems to me a rehash of Samo Burja's "Live vs Dead Players" (can you think/do new things or merely imitate) or even "thinking from first principles (can you investigate mechanisms or merely imitate). 

Like, I was at Ye's concert in the Algarve right and it was really poorly organized. I was in a line of Ye knows how many cars that didn't move for 40 minutes. I got out of the car, told everyone behind me to back up and turn the car around go over the sidewalk and exit from the back and they did and it worked. Those who were ahead of me are probably still there.

Now, was that a "high agency" move? I mean — sure. But I feel particularly empowered to take charge in situations like these, for some reason (Portugal) they keep happening, it worked once, and each further success heightens my confidence. So am I "high agency" tout court? Idk man, last year I was randomly (spiritual path[?]) afraid of taking planes? Like it just feels like a faulty abstraction. 

I can *see* why it went viral (same reason as "Live vs Dead Players" — people looooooove new ways to say good vs bad [chad/virgin, diamond/coal, …]) but idk I just don't think it's super useful.

Oxford philosopher Timothy Williamson says we attribute mental states when belief and desire best explain behavior.

Once AI systems gain autonomy and real-world interaction, denying them the same standard may no longer make sense. https://t.co/YINpiMtHKX

p.x: This is an interview with Oxford’s Timothy Williamson. He’s one of the most cited living philosophers, and simultaneously one of the most controversial (yet respected). He dismantles physicalism, solipsism, and reductionism––explaining why consciousness is philosophically overrated and why AI in its current form likely lacks genuine mental states. This will be a tour‐de‐force episode into all things related to looking deeply and fundamentally. If you’re interested in consciousness, free will, art, language, and meaning, I believe you’ll love this episode.
